findings.finding: The all-true C01 booleans are not complete machine differentiation/normalization certificates. Wolfram tests the literal first entry of du={0,v1,v2,v3}; SymPy begins from the supplied projected differentiated system; Sage defines grad_u=-L.inverse()*D before checking its residual. Sage C03 order/equality reasoning and part of C04 Euler/EOS reasoning also live in the companion derivation, not in the boolean alone.
findings.consequence: A claim that these engines independently machine-proved every step would overstate coverage. The explicit SymPy and Sage companion derivations do supply the missing elementary product-rule/normalization/projection and ordered-real reasoning; they can be reviewed as mixed mathematical proofs with exact CAS certificates. They are not kernel formalizations or a replacement for the xAct-specific missing obligation in F1.
